findings.title: Delivery registration and device copy of 1531/1532 outlive the map object: use-after-free writes into the shared segment, and stale state on a re-created map
findings.scenario: Case 1: a libbpf tool using a 1531/1532 map exits (Ctrl-C, skel__destroy) while the traced CUDA app keeps running. Its close goes close_fd -> clear_id_at -> map_free -> memory.destroy_ptr(impl) (map_handler.cpp:1664-1668). Nothing removes the map from gpu_model's registry, so the agent's delivery thread keeps calling m.map->host_words() / status_words() on the destroyed object every 200 ms (sum) or 2 s (per-thread), and once more in the atexit final delivery. After the free, the allocator's free-tree hooks overwrite the first bytes of the impl, and data_buffer is its first member. host_words() then decodes to another free block or to nullptr. Every word that differs from the snapshot gets written there: the segment's free tree is corrupted, or the write through NULL crashes the host process with SIGSEGV. A per-thread map writes up to the whole grid copy, e.g. 32 MB. Case 2: auto-refresh or a second tool session against the same app re-creates the map, and the boost allocator very likely returns the same block for a same-size object. The process-local `made` cache matches on the raw pointer and returns the old device buffer without setting `shards`, which is 0 in the new object. get_gpu_map_max_thread_count() is then 0 and sum_array_offset returns NULL, so every GPU add is dropped. Meanwhile the old registration keeps delivering the old buffer's sums into the new object, so the new tool reads the previous session's counts as current. If the new 1532 map has more entries or threads than the old one, the GPU indexes past the old device allocation, and the old registration copies the old geometry's word count into a possibly smaller new data_buffer, overflowing it in shared memory.
findings.evidence: nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:505-511: `static std::vector<std::pair<nv_gpu_device_array_map_impl *, CUdeviceptr> > made; ... for (auto &[m, d] : made) if (m == this) return d;` (returns before `shards = s` at 526). register_device_array (433-480) stores `registered_map m{ map, device, ... }` with a raw pointer and takes no map_refcnt reference. deliver_locked 316-333: `uint64_t *dst = m.map->host_words(); ... __atomic_store_n(&dst[i], v, ...)`, `uint64_t *st = m.map->status_words(); __atomic_fetch_add(&st[GPU_MODEL_STATUS_DELIVERIES], 1, ...)`. map_handler.cpp:1664-1668 destroys the impl with no deregistration. There is no unregister function at all.
findings.fix: Take a shared reference (inc_map_refcount / map_refcnt_ptr) for each registration and release it on unregister. Alternatively, have map_free (or the handler's close in the agent) call gpu_model::unregister(impl) under run_mutex before destroy_ptr, and drop the `made` entry and free the device buffer and staging. Key the `made` cache by (handler id, a generation number stored in the impl at construction), not by the raw address. Keep `shards` in the process-local `made` record and read it from there.

findings.title: 1530 values are generic addresses into .local, and an eBPF atomic add on them is undefined per the PTX ISA
findings.scenario: A CUDA eBPF program does `__sync_fetch_and_add(&v->cnt, 1)` on a value looked up from a 1530 thread-local map. This is the usual libbpf counter idiom, and it is also what a program written for 1531 must do, so switching a map from 1531 to 1530 keeps it. llvmbpf lowers BPF_ATOMIC ADD to a generic `atom.add.u64 [%rdN]`; the step0b C1 pass output (b_pass_output.ptx:271) shows exactly this right after `call _bpf_helper_ext_0001`. Through helper 1, or the routing's direct-lookup address, %rdN is a cvta.local address. The PTX ISA allows scalar atom only on .global/.shared or on generic addresses that point there. The result is undefined; on hardware it typically raises an illegal-address fault, which is sticky for the application's CUDA context and kills the host's GPU work. Nothing in the trampoline, the routing or the program load rejects or rewrites it.
findings.evidence: thread_local_offset: `return (char *)(uintptr_t)area + (uintptr_t)info.extra_buffer + idx * info.value_size;`. helper 1 at 283-286 returns it as the lookup result. PTX ISA 9.7.15.5 (docs/text/ptx-isa.txt, atom description): "atom with scalar type may be used only with .global and .shared spaces and with generic addressing, where the address points to .global or .shared space." There are no atom, XADD or isspacep checks in nv_thread_local_routing.cpp.
findings.fix: At load time, refuse (with a counted, logged reason) CUDA programs whose BPF_ATOMIC instructions can address a 1530 value: track r0 from helper-1 calls and direct lookups on 1530 fds. Alternatively, in the PTX post-pass, rewrite each generic atom in routed probe functions behind `isspacep.local` into a plain ld/op/st. The copy is thread-private, so this is exact. Document that 1530 values take plain arithmetic only.

findings.title: "Atomic adds only" for 1531/1532 is assumed, not checked: plain stores lose counts, and 32-bit adds make mixed-size races with the snapshot
findings.scenario: Helper 1 hands the program a plain writable pointer into the 1531 shard or the 1532 slot, and bpftime has no verifier. (a) A program written like the shipped threadhist example (`*cnt += 1`, a non-atomic ld/add/st) on a 1531 map: every warp of an SM shares the (SM, lane) shard, so concurrent read-modify-writes from different warps on one SM lose increments, and the CPU sees too-low sums silently. (b) A 32-bit atomic add (BPF_W XADD, e.g. a value struct of two u32 counters with value_size 8) on a 1531/1532 word overlaps the snapshot's 64-bit ld.relaxed.gpu only partially. Per PTX 8.7 these are not morally strong (that requires complete overlap), so this is a mixed-size data race, and "the axioms in the memory consistency model do not apply" to the program. In addition, summing the u64 words over shards carries the low u32's overflow into the high u32 field. (c) Plain stores to 1532 from two concurrent kernels with the same thread index race with each other and with the delivery reads. The commit's 'no data race' claim and the rule that correctness rests only on documented guarantees therefore hold only for programs nobody checks.
findings.evidence: default_trampoline.cu:288-299 returns `sum_array_offset(...)` / `array_map_offset(...)` pointers. The only enforcement is in helper 2 (368-370: `return (uint64_t)-1` for update) and in the CPU-side elem_update (EPERM). nv_gpu_model_maps.hpp:10-11: "which GPU programs may change with 64-bit atomic adds only (XADD)". The snapshot reads `ld.relaxed.gpu.u64` (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:177). example/gpu/threadhist/threadhist.bpf.c:27 uses `*cnt += 1`.
findings.fix: At CUDA program load, track pointers derived from helper-1 results on 1531/1532 fds and accept only BPF_ATOMIC|BPF_ADD|BPF_DW (with or without FETCH) stores through them, plus loads. Refuse other stores and narrower atomics with a logged reason. Alternatively, replace the pointer with a dedicated add helper (map, key, delta) that performs the 64-bit atom.add itself.

findings.title: Several GPU processes on one segment overwrite each other's delivered values, and the shard count is shared across processes
findings.scenario: Two CUDA processes run under the same tool session (two `bpftime start` apps, or a multi-process app such as worker processes on one GPU). Each allocates its own device copy and registers its own delivery into the same shared data_buffer. The CPU then reads whichever process delivered last: process A's sums or B's, never A+B. The PID status word flips, and FINAL=1 from the first process to exit is overwritten by the other's later deliveries. Nothing detects or logs this. If the processes run on GPUs whose SM counts round to different powers of two, B's `shards = s` overwrites the shared field. Any later create_map_basic_info in A then returns B's larger shard count with A's smaller device buffer, so A's GPU adds index past its allocation (out-of-bounds device writes).
findings.evidence: `shards = s;` writes the member of the shared-memory object (526); get_max_thread_count() returns `per_thread ? thread_count : shards`. The header comment admits the assumption: "(one GPU process per segment; 0 until then)". deliver_locked writes `m.map->host_words()` and `status_words()` in the shared object from every registered process.
findings.fix: Keep the shard count per process (in the `made` record) and pass that to map_info. Claim the map for one delivering process: CAS the PID status word from 0 or a dead PID to getpid() at registration. In other processes, refuse with a logged error and return 0, so their programs get NULL. Alternatively, keep a per-process delivered copy and sum the copies on CPU lookups.

findings.title: No creation checks for 1530/1531/1532: other key sizes and 0 entries are accepted and handled as 4-byte array keys
findings.scenario: check_map_attr's switch has no case for the new types (default: return 0), so creation accepts any key_size and max_entries 0. With key_size 1 or 2, a tool's bpf(BPF_MAP_GET_NEXT_KEY) through the syscall server writes 4 bytes into libbpf's key_size-byte next_key buffer, a heap overflow in the tool, and lookups read 4 bytes past the key. With key_size 8, keys >= 2^32 alias entry (key mod 2^32) on both GPU and CPU instead of failing. With max_entries 0, get_next_key(NULL) returns key 0 and a lookup of key 0 then returns status word 0 (the delivery count) as if it were a value. The kernel refuses all of these for arrays (EINVAL).
findings.evidence: array_next_key: `auto &next = *(uint32_t *)next_key; if (key == nullptr || *(const uint32_t *)key >= entries) { next = 0; return 0; }`. elem_lookup: `auto k = *(const uint32_t *)key; if (k >= max_entries && k < max_entries + GPU_MODEL_STATUS_WORDS)`. map_handler.cpp check_map_attr only covers HASH/ARRAY/PERCPU/QUEUE/STACK, and map_init_checked 1493-1517 constructs the new types unchecked.
findings.fix: Add 1530/1531/1532 to the ARRAY case of check_map_attr (max_entries > 0, key_size == 4, value_size > 0; for 1531/1532 also value_size % 8 == 0 there instead of throwing in the constructor). Also include the per-thread copy count in the size bound for 1532.

notes:
I reviewed everything read-only: no build, no runs, no files written. The advisor call timed out, so these findings have not had a second review.

Checks that came out fine:
- **Sum-map shard index:** it stays in bounds whatever value the SM id register returns. It is masked with (power of two - 1), and both buffers use that same power of two times 32. The PTX ISA says the SM id may be non-contiguous and may change while a thread runs; this affects only which shard a thread uses, never correctness.
- **Lane id:** using it as an index relies on the documented 32-thread warp (CUDA guide: "groups of 32"; warp size 32 for every compute capability).
- **Layouts:** the 1531 layout [entry][shard][value] matches the snapshot's (e*S+s)*W+w. The 1532 layout matches array_map_offset and the delivery's W = thread_count*value_size/8.
- **Status keys:** lookups of keys max_entries+0..7 stay inside status_buffer (64 + thread_count*value_size bytes).
- **Null buffers:** a null extra_buffer, or a shard count of 0 or below 32, makes the helpers return NULL or 0. A failed allocation leaves extra_buffer null before the shard count is read.
- **Older map types:** the new checks are separate type-equality branches, so old types behave as before. The regenerated trampoline_ptx.h keeps .version 8.1 / sm_61 and only re-numbers registers and reorders branches. The new paths read param_4 for 1530.
- **1530 offset in extra_buffer:** the first map's offset is 0, but nothing for type 1530 treats extra_buffer==nullptr as "no buffer".
- **Size arithmetic:** cannot overflow in practice; the shared-memory allocation bounds max_entries*value_size (and thread_count) first.
- **Return codes:** the helper 2/3 values (-1) match the existing ordinary-array GPU path's convention.

Not reported because the behaviour already exists in 1502: the device printf warning for out-of-range 1532 threads (it writes to the host's stdout, against the host-process contract), and the 32-bit integer arithmetic in getGlobalThreadId.

findings.title: Closing a 1531/1532 map frees it while the delivery thread keeps writing through a raw pointer (use-after-free in the shared segment)
findings.scenario: A tool loads a program using a 1531 sum map and the CUDA app runs under the agent. The tool exits normally: Ctrl-C, then skeleton destroy, then close(map_fd). The CUDA app keeps running. The syscall server's handle_close calls bpftime_close, then close_fd, then clear_id_at, then map_free. The refcount drops from 1 to 0 and destroy_ptr frees the impl, its data_buffer and its status_buffer. Every 20 ms to 2 s, for the rest of the app's life, the agent's drain thread still calls m.map->host_words() and m.map->status_words() on the freed object. It writes n delivered words plus the status words into segment memory that the allocator has freed (and may already use for its free-block bookkeeping) or has handed to new objects, such as the next tool session's maps or perf shards. Result: segment corruption, and possibly a crash of the traced app or the tool. Also, get_gpu_mem_buffer's per-process cache is keyed by the impl address. A new map later constructed at the same address gets the old device buffer (old size) and no new registration, while the old registration writes the old geometry's n words into the new map.
findings.evidence: registered_map holds `nv_gpu_device_array_map_impl *map;` (cpp:193) and no reference is taken. deliver_locked does `uint64_t *dst = m.map->host_words();` (cpp:316) and `uint64_t *st = m.map->status_words();` (cpp:326). get_gpu_mem_buffer caches `for (auto &[m, d] : made) if (m == this) return d;` (cpp:509-511). The close path is syscall_context.cpp:295 `bpftime_close(fd);`, then handler_manager.cpp:123 `...map_free(memory);`, then map_handler.cpp map_free `fetch_sub(1)` and `memory.destroy_ptr(...)` (the refcount is initialised to 1 by init_refcnt). Nothing unregisters a map.
findings.fix: At registration, take a shared reference to the map impl as array_map_binding does (share_map_impl_from + inc_map_refcount under map_binding_mutex), so a tool's close cannot destroy it while this process delivers. Alternatively, before each delivery, check under map_binding_mutex that the handler still holds the same impl, and drop the registration and its `made` entry if it does not. Key `made` by something that cannot be reused (impl plus a generation), not by the address alone.

findings.title: cudaDeviceReset / primary-context reset is not handled: device copies and staging are freed, the final delivery fails and FINAL is never set
findings.scenario: A CUDA app ends main with cudaDeviceReset() (a common CUDA-samples idiom) and returns. The reset destroys the primary context's state, even though the agent retained it: the 1531/1532 device copies (cuMemAlloc, cpp:530), the pinned staging buffers (cuMemAllocHost, cpp:452), the snapshot module and the stream. At exit, deliver_now(true) launches s.fn from the destroyed module, logs 'snapshot failed' and sets broken, and FINAL is never set. Everything since the last periodic delivery is lost. A 1532 map is first due 1 s after registration (then every 1 s), so an app that runs under about 1 s gets no per-thread values at all. Sum maps lose up to the last 20 to 200 ms. Not verified, but possible: the drain thread can be inside its copy loop reading m.staging (cpp:318-324) when the reset frees that pinned memory, and if the app keeps using CUDA after the reset, probed kernels still receive the freed device pointers through map_basic_info.
findings.evidence: The CUDA guide says 'cudaDeviceReset destroys the primary context of the current device' (cpg-intro-to-cuda-cpp.txt:721) and 'cudaDeviceReset also frees all allocations' (cpg-writing-cuda-kernels.txt:276). No hook exists: a grep for DeviceReset, PrimaryCtxReset or cuCtxDestroy in attach/ and runtime/ finds only an unrelated cuCtxDestroy in bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:596. The final path is `int n = gpu_model::deliver_now(true);` (cpp:418), and on failure deliver_locked does `s.broken = true; return UINT64_MAX;` (cpp:310-314).
findings.fix: Hook cudaDeviceReset, cuDevicePrimaryCtxReset and cuCtxDestroy (the agent already interposes driver entry points). Before forwarding the call: take run_mutex, run the final delivery (this is still inside main, the documented window), mark the device copies and the `made` cache invalid, stop the drain thread, and have later probed loads get NULL buffers or freshly allocated ones.

findings.title: The final delivery sets FINAL=1 without waiting for application GPU work, so counts can be incomplete
findings.scenario: Three cases: (a) the app launches probed kernels on several streams, synchronizes only the stream it reads results from, then returns from main; (b) the app launches fire-and-forget work and exits; (c) a second app thread is still launching probed kernels when main calls exit(). The final snapshot runs on the agent's own CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING stream, which is ordered after no application work. It reads the shards of unfinished kernels, stores the values and sets FINAL=1. Adds from kernels that complete afterwards, or that start before _exit, are never delivered, while the status says the final delivery completed. A tool that waits for FINAL=1 reports undercounts as final. The header promises 'after the application synchronized', but nothing checks this.
findings.evidence: hpp:127-128: `A final delivery runs at process exit (atexit), after the application synchronized.` The stream is `cuStreamCreate(&s.stream, CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING)` (cpp:249), and drv-stream.txt:569 says a non-blocking stream performs 'no implicit synchronization with stream 0'. The final path launches at once (cpp:303-307) and then `if (final) __atomic_store_n(&st[GPU_MODEL_STATUS_FINAL], 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);` (cpp:331-333). There is no wait on launch_activity events and no context synchronize.
findings.fix: Before the final snapshot, wait with a bound for the probed launches the agent noted (the launch_activity events), and set FINAL=1 only when all of them completed. Otherwise store a distinct status (for example FINAL=2, 'final, possibly incomplete') and count it. Launches the hooks cannot note (graphs, unresolved handles) cannot be proven complete, so they should also give the 'possibly incomplete' status, unless the app's own synchronization was observed.

findings.title: The final delivery calls the driver API after main, which the CUDA guide says is undefined behaviour; FINAL rests on it
findings.scenario: Every normal process exit runs final_delivery_at_exit from atexit. It sets the context (cuCtxSetCurrent), may load and JIT the snapshot module (prepare_locked, when the app ran under 20 ms), launches a kernel and synchronizes a stream, all during program termination. The CUDA documents state that the runtime and driver use global state destroyed during termination, and that using them then is undefined. That the final delivery works, and therefore the FINAL=1 claim, rests only on measured behaviour and on atexit ordering against cudart's teardown, which the code itself calls 'not guaranteed'. This breaks the rule that correctness may rest only on documented guarantees.
findings.evidence: cpg-legacy-12.9.txt:2368: 'The CUDA interfaces use global state that is initialized during host program initiation and destroyed during host program termination. The CUDA runtime and driver cannot detect if this state is invalid, so using any of these interfaces ... during program initiation or termination after main) will result in undefined behavior.' (also cpg-intro-to-cuda-cpp.txt:725). In the code, cpp:474-477: `// after the application's cudart registered its own exit handler? Not guaranteed; ...` then `atexit(final_delivery_at_exit);`.
findings.fix: Make the last guaranteed delivery happen inside main: deliver from hooks on the app's synchronizing and teardown calls (cuCtxSynchronize/cudaDeviceSynchronize, rate-limited; cudaDeviceReset; cuCtxDestroy; cuDevicePrimaryCtxRelease) and record that status. Keep the atexit delivery only as a best-effort extra that is reported with a different status value, never as FINAL=1.

findings.title: The exit-time final delivery waits without bound, so an app exiting while a GPU-filling kernel runs can hang
findings.scenario: An app runs a persistent kernel that occupies every SM and loops until a host flag is set, or any long kernel. Its main thread calls exit() without stopping it (for example from a Ctrl-C handler). Without the agent, the process ends and the driver tears the context down. With the agent, final_delivery_at_exit joins the drain thread, which may be blocked in cuStreamSynchronize on a snapshot kernel that cannot be scheduled. It then launches the final snapshot and calls cuStreamSynchronize itself. Concurrent kernel execution is not guaranteed, so the snapshot may never run: exit() hangs forever, or for as long as the app's kernel runs. This breaks the host-process contract.
findings.evidence: cpp:416-417: `if (s.thread.joinable()) s.thread.join();`. cpp:306-307: `if (r == CUDA_SUCCESS) r = cuStreamSynchronize(s.stream);` (no deadline, also on the final path). cpg-lazy-loading.txt:247: 'Some programs incorrectly assume that concurrent kernel execution is guaranteed. A deadlock can occur ...'.
findings.fix: At exit, never block without a bound. Signal stop, then wait for the drain thread with a deadline (a condition variable plus an 'in delivery' flag instead of join). For the final snapshot, poll cuStreamQuery up to a deadline (for example 1 s) instead of calling cuStreamSynchronize. On timeout, give up, do not set FINAL, and count the skip. Optionally also bound the drain thread's own waits.

findings.title: Fork children inherit the delivery state and the atexit handler: a child can hang at exit or call CUDA with the parent's context
findings.scenario: A CUDA app forks a worker that later calls exit(), for example a child doing CPU-side work. The child inherits state() (s.ctx, s.maps, s.thread, the mutexes) and the atexit registration, and nothing marks it as a child. The drain thread holds run_mutex for a whole delivery: snapshot launch, synchronize and copy. For a 32 MB per-thread map the copy alone takes milliseconds every second, and the first prepare compiles the PTX (about 240 ms). If the fork lands inside that window, the child's run_mutex (or wake_mutex at cpp:412) stays locked forever, and the child's exit() blocks at deliver_now: a host process hangs. Otherwise the child runs context_scope and cuLaunchKernel with the parent's context. No documented guarantee covers this. If those calls succeeded, the child would write PID=child, deliveries and FINAL=1 into the parent's shared maps while the parent is still running.
findings.evidence: drain_loop holds the lock over the whole delivery: `std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(s.run_mutex); ... due = deliver_locked(s, false, nullptr);` (cpp:401-404). deliver_now: `context_scope scope(s.ctx); std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(s.run_mutex);` (cpp:487-488). The handler is registered with `atexit(final_delivery_at_exit);` (cpp:477). The file has no fork handler and no owner-pid check.
findings.fix: Record the owner pid at the first registration. Register a child handler through bpftime::register_fork_handlers (not pthread_atfork, per CLAUDE.md) that marks the state as inherited. In final_delivery_at_exit and deliver_now, return at once when getpid() != owner pid, before touching any mutex, the std::thread or CUDA.

findings.title: The one-GPU-process-per-segment assumption is not enforced: two agent processes overwrite each other's delivered values and FINAL
findings.scenario: A tool loads a 1531 map, and two CUDA processes run with the agent on the same segment. Examples: two `bpftime start` runs, or an app whose children inherit LD_PRELOAD (multi-process training or serving workers). Each process allocates its own device copy, registers its own delivery, and writes its own shard sums into the same shared data_buffer. The tool sees one process's count at a time, alternating, never their sum, and the status PID flips. The first process to exit sets FINAL=1, then the other keeps overwriting the values with its own partial counts. The results are silently wrong, and nothing is logged.
findings.evidence: hpp:65-66: `// 1531: shards per key, set by the agent that allocated the device copy (one GPU process per segment; 0 until then)`. cpp:319-322 does `if (__atomic_load_n(&dst[i], __ATOMIC_RELAXED) != v) { __atomic_store_n(&dst[i], v, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);` into the shared host_words(). PID and FINAL are stored unconditionally (cpp:327-333). get_gpu_mem_buffer and register_device_array claim nothing in shared memory.
findings.fix: At the first get_gpu_mem_buffer of a map, claim it in shared memory with a CAS of an owner field (pid plus a start time). A second process logs once, counts the refusal and returns 0 (the GPU helpers then return NULL), or it gets its own value area. Alternatively, sum per-process contributions on the CPU side.

findings.title: '64-bit atomic adds only' is not enforced: 32-bit XADD, plain read-modify-write stores and other atomics silently corrupt or undercount 1531/1532 values
findings.scenario:
Lookups of 1531 and 1532 return a writable pointer, and nothing checks how the program uses it.
(a) A value like `struct { u32 hits; u32 inflight; }` (value_size 8 passes the %8 check), updated with `__sync_fetch_and_add(&v->inflight, ±1)`, is lowered to a 32-bit atom.add. It partially overlaps the snapshot's 64-bit ld.relaxed.gpu, so the two are not morally strong: a mixed-size data race, for which the PTX consistency axioms do not apply. Summing u64 words over shards also carries between packed fields: +1 in one shard and -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) in another give 0x1_00000000, so 'inflight' reads 0 and 'hits' gains 1.
(b) The common PERCPU_ARRAY idiom `if (v) *v += 1;` (plain load, add, store) loses increments, because every warp on an SM shares that SM's 32 lane shards, and 1532 slots are shared by concurrent kernels with the same thread index. The result is silent undercounting.
(c) Atomic OR, XCHG or CMPXCHG values are summed over shards, which gives meaningless numbers.
findings.evidence: default_trampoline.cu:288-299 returns `sum_array_offset(real_key, map_info)` / `array_map_offset(...)` as a writable pointer. Only helper 2 (update) is refused (lines 368-370). A grep for 1531, 1532, GPU_SUM_ARRAY or DEVICE_PER_THREAD in attach/, vm/ and runtime/ finds no check anywhere else (routing, pass or VM). vm/llvm-jit/src/compiler.cpp:1637-1647 lowers EBPF_ATOMIC_OPCODE_32 adds as 32-bit atomicrmw (`inst.opcode == EBPF_ATOMIC_OPCODE_64` selects the width). ptx-isa.txt:7371 requires 'If both are memory operations, then they overlap completely' for moral strength, and 7385 says 'The axioms ... do not apply if a PTX program contains one or more mixed-size data-races.' The claim it breaks is hpp:11: 'GPU programs may change with 64-bit atomic adds only (XADD)'.
findings.fix: At load time (the PTX pass or prepare), check that every use of a pointer returned by a lookup of a 1531/1532 map is a BPF_ATOMIC|BPF_DW BPF_ADD (no fetch needed) at an 8-byte-aligned offset below value_size, with no other load, store or atomic through it. Refuse the program (logged and counted) when it does not comply. Until then, document 1531/1532 as accepting only that instruction.

findings.title: Device-copy allocation runs on the link-instantiating thread in global capture mode with a NULL-stream memset (capture invalidation on injected or late attach)
findings.scenario: The agent is injected into a running process (`bpftime attach <pid>`), or a CUDA link is instantiated later, while an app thread is capturing a CUDA graph on a blocking stream (llama.cpp captures graphs repeatedly). create_map_basic_info then calls get_gpu_mem_buffer on the agent's thread in the default (global) mode, and it calls cuMemAlloc, cuMemsetD8 on the NULL stream, and cuMemAllocHost. The NULL-stream memset forms a disallowed implicit dependency on the capturing blocking stream, which invalidates the app's capture, so its EndCapture/instantiate fails and many apps abort on that. The cuMemAlloc call is a prohibited unsafe call under another thread's global-mode capture. The drain thread switches to relaxed mode, but this path does not. (Preloaded agents instantiate before main and are not affected.)
findings.evidence: cpp:530-531: `if (cuMemAlloc(&d, bytes) != CUDA_SUCCESS || cuMemsetD8(d, 0, bytes) != CUDA_SUCCESS)`. cpp:452: `cuMemAllocHost((void **)&m.staging, bytes)`. Neither is wrapped in cuThreadExchangeStreamCaptureMode, unlike context_scope (cpp:369). drv-types.txt:6561: CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_IMPLICIT 'indicates a disallowed implicit dependency on a current capture sequence from cudaStreamLegacy'.
findings.fix: Wrap the allocation in a relaxed capture-mode scope (as context_scope does). Zero the memory with cuMemsetD8Async on the agent's own non-blocking stream instead of the NULL stream, followed by a cuStreamSynchronize of that stream.

findings.title: The device copy's zeroing is not ordered before its first use: memset on the NULL stream, asynchronous, pointer published at once
findings.scenario: cuMemsetD8 on device memory returns before the zeroing is done, and the pointer goes straight into map_basic_info and the delivery registration. Probed kernels on non-blocking app streams (ggml-cuda creates its streams non-blocking) and the snapshot kernel (also non-blocking) are not ordered after NULL-stream work. In the late or injected path, where the legacy stream can sit behind long work on the app's blocking streams, a probed kernel can add before the memset runs, and the memset then zeroes those adds (lost counts). The snapshot can also read uninitialised cuMemAlloc memory and deliver garbage. Zero initialisation therefore rests on timing, not on a documented ordering.
findings.evidence: cpp:531: `cuMemsetD8(d, 0, bytes)`, then cpp:541-544 `made.emplace_back(this, d); gpu_model::register_device_array(...); return d;`. drv-api-sync.txt:63: 'The cudaMemset functions are asynchronous with respect to the host except when the target memory is pinned host memory.' drv-stream.txt:569: a CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING stream 'should perform no implicit synchronization with stream 0'.
findings.fix: Zero with cuMemsetD8Async on the agent's own stream and cuStreamSynchronize that stream (or synchronize CU_STREAM_LEGACY) before returning or publishing the pointer.

findings.title: A status-key lookup returns status words i..7 rather than 'status word i then zeros', breaking the documented status read for wide or per-thread values
findings.scenario: A tool reads key max_entries+1 (FINAL) of a 1531 map with value_size 16 and gets {final, pid}, not {final, 0}. For a 1532 map (value = value_size × thread_count through bpf()), key max_entries+0 returns deliveries as tid 0, final as tid 1 and pid as tid 2. A tool that handles the value like any 1502-style per-thread value (sums over threads) reads 'deliveries' as deliveries+final+pid. A tool that checks the whole value against {1,0,...} never sees FINAL.
findings.evidence: hpp:16-18: `A lookup of key max_entries + i returns status word i (then zeros up to a value)`. cpp:100: `return status_buffer.data() + 8 * (k - max_entries);`. The bpf() copy takes get_userspace_value_size() bytes from that pointer (map_handler.cpp:77-104, which multiplies by gpu_thread_count for 1532).
findings.fix: Give each status word a value-sized slot: either size status_buffer as GPU_MODEL_STATUS_WORDS × userspace value size, with word i at the start of slot i, or copy word i (with an acquire load) into a zeroed per-thread buffer and return that.

notes:
Checked and found correct, so not reported: the snapshot kernel's indexing matches both device layouts. For 1531 the trampoline writes at (idx*S + shard)*value_size and the kernel reads (e*S+s)*W+w with W = value_size/8. For 1532, S=1 and the [key][tid] layout matches array_map_offset. The grid-stride loop, the 64-bit div/rem by W (n=0 whenever W=0) and the n=0 warm-up launch with null pointers are fine (the loop never runs). Each map has its own pinned staging buffer, written only by its snapshot under run_mutex and read only after stream sync, so it is never reused across maps or deliveries. Registration and delivery handle the append-only s.maps index correctly under reg_mutex. A constructor throw (value_size not a multiple of 8) is caught by map_init and becomes EINVAL; Boost frees the partial construction. Status-key lookups stay in bounds for both 1531 and 1532 (status_buffer is 64 + thread_count*value_size). atexit ordering against the app's __cudaUnregisterBinaryUtil is fine: the agent registers after the app's constructors, so its handler runs first. Logging goes through spdlog (no direct stdio), and std::thread failure is caught by the agent's try around init_attach_ctx_from_handlers.

Left out as theoretical or minor: the acquire fence at cpp:99 sits before the caller's plain read of FINAL, so seeing FINAL=1 does not formally order later value reads (C++ model only). key_size is not checked to be 4 for 1530/1531/1532. The drain thread and the exit-time delivery do not call ignore_probes_on_this_thread, so their mallocs and syscalls are visible to CPU probes (the existing CUDA watcher thread does not either). When the staging allocation fails, the device copy is still returned and used but never delivered; only an error is logged and deliveries stays 0. A 1532 map on a device below sm_70 is never delivered: the snapshot PTX targets sm_70, prepare fails and logs.

findings.title: An atomic add on a 1530 thread-local value becomes a generic atom on local memory, which PTX does not define, and nothing rejects it
findings.scenario: A tool keeps a per-thread counter with the usual libbpf/BCC idiom: `u64 *c = bpf_map_lookup_elem(&tl_counts, &zero); if (c) __sync_fetch_and_add(c, 1);`. This is likely when someone switches an existing 1502 counter map to 1530. The lookup becomes the direct form `selp.b64 r, %bptl_a, 0, p`, where %bptl_a is the cvta.local area address plus the offset. The XADD is lowered by llvmbpf's emitAtomicBinOp (vm/llvm-jit/src/compiler_utils.cpp:376, CreateAtomicRMW, Monotonic) to a generic `atom.add.u64 [r], 1`. The same lowering is visible on a 1531 pointer in lat4 6lQrMe patched.temp.1.sm_87.ptx:2678. Here r points into the local window, which is outside the documented use of atom. The result is undefined: the probed kernel may fault (an illegal-address or illegal-instruction error kills the application's kernel and leaves its CUDA context unusable, which ends the host process), or the add may work by accident. The non-direct path (default_trampoline.cu:249 thread_local_offset, returned at :285) leads to the same thing. Neither the routing pass, the trampoline nor the loader checks for it, and the commit's checks only used plain loads and stores (the C1 carry).
findings.evidence: PTX ISA 9.7.15.5 atom (ptx-isa.txt:26571): "atom with scalar type may be used only with .global and .shared spaces and with generic addressing, where the address points to .global or .shared space." The same rule holds for red (27027). Routing code: `<< "\tselp.b64 \t" << rm[1].str() << ", %bptl_a" << n << ", 0, %bptl_p" << n` with `add.u64 %bptl_a, %bptl_a, %bpftime_tl_in`. The area address comes from `cvta.local.u64 %bpftime_tl, __bpftime_tl` (lines 309, 328). The header (nv_thread_local_routing.hpp:13-16) claims correctness rests on documented guarantees and names only local memory as the thread's storage.
findings.fix: In route_function_body (routed functions only), rewrite every generic atom.*/red.* so a documented test picks the path: `isspacep.local p, addr`. If p, do a plain ld/op/st, which is equivalent because the storage is private to the thread. Otherwise run the original atom. Alternatively, reject at load time any program whose 1530 lookup result (constant fd, tracked through moves and adds) reaches BPF_STX|BPF_ATOMIC. In that case fail the routing so the original image loads, and log and count the refusal.

findings.title: The 1531/1532 'atomic adds only' contract that the no-data-race claim depends on is not enforced; plain or 32-bit accesses are mixed-size races
findings.scenario: (i) 1532, the per-thread map. Helper 2 is refused, so users write through the lookup pointer, e.g. `*v = bpf_ktime_get_ns()`. In this build a 64-bit eBPF store through a map-value pointer is emitted as two st.u32 (pass output 6lQrMe:2755-2757). The snapshot's `ld.relaxed.gpu.u64` overlaps them only partly. That is a mixed-size data race: the CPU can receive a torn value (new high half, old low half), and under PTX the memory-model axioms then stop applying to the whole program. (ii) 1531, the sum map, with `(*v)++` (the BCC idiom without __sync): this is a weak read-modify-write. Every warp on an SM shares the same 32 lane shards (shard = (smid & mask)*32 + laneid), so concurrent warps lose increments and the delivered sums are silently low. Any read of the counter by a program (`if (*v > N)`, two ld.u32 as at 6lQrMe:2582-2583) is also a mixed-size race with the other threads' atom.add.u64. (iii) 1531 with value_size 8 used as two u32 fields and 32-bit XADDs: atom.add.u32 partially overlaps the snapshot's u64 load (a mixed-size race). The u64 shard sum also carries the low field into the high one: shard A low=0xFFFFFFFF plus shard B low=1 is delivered as low 0, high +1. Nothing checks programs for any of this.
findings.evidence: Comment and code: `// changed with atomic adds only (a plain store would race with the delivery's reads)`, with helper 2 returning -1 for 1531/1532 (366-370). Helper 1 still returns a raw writable pointer (`return (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)sum_array_offset(...)` :290, `array_map_offset` for 1532). PTX 8.7: morally strong requires "each operation is strong and specifies a scope that includes the thread executing the other operation" and "If both are memory operations, then they overlap completely." PTX 8.7.2: "The axioms in the memory consistency model do not apply if a PTX program contains one or more mixed-size data-races." PTX 8.10: "Atomicity is not guaranteed if the operations are not morally strong." The claim holds only for XADD.DW, lowered to `atom.add.u64` (default .relaxed and .gpu, ptx-isa.txt:26577/26579).
findings.fix: Enforce the contract at load or attach time. Track pointers returned by helper 1 for a constant 1531/1532 fd, as constant_fd already does, and refuse any access other than BPF_STX|BPF_ATOMIC|BPF_DW with BPF_ADD at an 8-byte-aligned offset: no plain loads or stores, no 32-bit atomics, and no passing the pointer to helpers such as probe_read. On refusal keep the original image and log and count it. Alternatively check in the PTX routing pass that every use of such a lookup result is atom.add.u64 or red.add.u64.

findings.title: The final delivery claim (g) fails when the application calls cudaDeviceReset before exit or exits with probed kernels in flight; FINAL=1 is set regardless
findings.scenario: (i) An application ends with `cudaDeviceSynchronize(); cudaDeviceReset(); return 0;`, which the guide suggests for flushing device printf. The reset destroys the primary context, so the 1531/1532 device buffers, the snapshot module and the stream are gone before the agent's atexit handler runs. Counts since the last periodic delivery are lost: up to 20 ms (200 ms when idle) for sum maps and 1-2 s for per-thread maps. The final snapshot fails (FINAL stays 0, logged). Meanwhile the drain thread keeps calling cuLaunchKernel and cuStreamSynchronize with handles of a destroyed context, which the documents do not define. (ii) An application launches probed kernels on a non-blocking stream and returns from main without synchronizing. The final snapshot synchronizes only its own CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING stream, so nothing orders it after those kernels. It may run before them or alongside them, and `GPU_MODEL_STATUS_FINAL` is still set to 1. The tool is told the delivery is final while those kernels' adds are never delivered. The commit says only "a final delivery at exit (atexit)"; the header's condition "after the application synchronized" is neither checked nor reflected in the status word.
findings.evidence: deliver_locked syncs only `s.stream` and then does `if (final) __atomic_store_n(&st[GPU_MODEL_STATUS_FINAL], 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);` (331-333). Nothing hooks cudaDeviceReset, cuDevicePrimaryCtxReset or cuCtxDestroy (git grep: none). CPG intro (cpg-intro-to-cuda-cpp.txt:721): "cudaDeviceReset destroys the primary context of the current device." CPG writing kernels (:276): "cudaDeviceReset also frees all allocations." CPG printf (cpg-cpp-language-support.txt:2392-2396): flushed on "Context destruction via cudaDeviceReset() or cuCtxDestroy()" and "the buffer is not automatically flushed when the program exits." PTX API synchronization gives edges only from the application's own `cudaStreamSynchronize`, event or device synchronization, or from stream order.
findings.fix: Hook cudaDeviceReset, cuDevicePrimaryCtxReset and cuCtxDestroy: stop the drain thread and run the final delivery before forwarding the call. At exit, make s.stream wait (cuStreamWaitEvent) on the launch-activity events of noted probed launches before the final snapshot. This is documented: "An event record task synchronizes with matching event wait tasks." Never call cuCtxSynchronize (step0b C5: crash). Publish a distinct status (e.g. FINAL=2, incomplete) when a noted event was still pending or unnoted launches such as graphs were seen.

findings.title: (Outside this dimension) A forked child that calls exit() hangs in the atexit handler joining the parent's delivery thread
findings.scenario: A traced CUDA process forks, and the child calls exit(): for example `exit(127)` after a failed exec, or a forked worker returning from main. The child runs final_delivery_at_exit. Its copied `s.thread` is joinable but the thread does not exist in the child, so `s.thread.join()` waits on the parent's thread descriptor tid, which nothing clears. If the drain thread held wake_mutex at the fork, the child blocks even earlier on that lock. Either way the child hangs for good, which breaks the host-process contract. Found by reading glibc's join semantics; not run.
findings.evidence: `if (s.thread.joinable()) s.thread.join(); int n = gpu_model::deliver_now(true);`. No fork handler resets `state()`: nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp has no register_fork_handlers call.
findings.fix: Record the owner pid in delivery_state. Register a child handler through bpftime::register_fork_handlers that marks the state foreign: release the std::thread object without joining it and reinitialize the mutexes. Make final_delivery_at_exit and deliver_now return at once when getpid() != owner.

findings.title: Device scope covers only one memory synchronization domain, so the 'morally strong' claims (c) and (d) lack a run-time check
findings.scenario: This cannot occur on the Orin (CC 8.7 reports one domain). On a CC >= 9.0 GPU (4 domains), probed kernels can run in another domain: NCCL >= 2.16 tags its launches with the remote domain, and a stream's domain map can send default launches to physical domain 1. The snapshot runs on s.stream in domain 0. Its `ld.relaxed.gpu` and the programs' `atom.add.u64` (.gpu) are then not related by device scope, so they are not morally strong, and 'no data race' and single-copy atomicity have no documentary support. Adds to the same 1531 shard from kernels in two domains also lose documented atomicity. The rule asks for a run-time check with a counted fallback, and there is none.
findings.evidence: CPG 5.8.1.1 (cpg-cuda-cpp-memory-model.txt:177): "Each GPU thread is related to each other GPU thread in the same CUDA device and within the same memory synchronization domain by the device thread scope". CPG 4.16.2: "ordering or synchronization between distinct domains on the same GPU requires system-scope fencing ... Note that this modifies the definition of thread_scope_device." CPG 4.16.3: "NCCL 2.16 will do so" and "CUDA will report a count of 1 on devices prior to compute capability 9.0." Code: `ld.relaxed.gpu.u64 %rd15, [%rd14];`.
findings.fix: In prepare_locked, query CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_SYNC_DOMAIN_COUNT. When it is greater than 1, turn off the periodic snapshot and deliver only after documented synchronization, logging and counting the change. Alternatively refuse 1531/1532 on that device.

findings.title: The zeroing memset is asynchronous on the legacy stream and nothing documented orders it before the snapshot or the probed kernels on non-blocking streams
findings.scenario: `cuMemsetD8(d, 0, bytes)` enqueues on the legacy stream and returns before the memset completes. The snapshot stream is CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING (line 249), and llama.cpp's streams are non-blocking. Only elapsed time orders the zeroing before the first snapshot (20 ms later) and before the programs' adds: microseconds against milliseconds, so in practice this never fails. The documents give no edge, though, and cuMemAlloc contents are unspecified. If the memset were still pending, the first delivery could report stale memory as counts, or the memset could overwrite early adds. The same pattern already exists in nv_gpu_per_thread_array_map.cpp:69.
findings.evidence: Driver API, API synchronization behavior (drv-api-sync.txt): "The cudaMemset functions are asynchronous with respect to the host except when the target memory is pinned host memory." Stream sync (drv-stream-sync.txt:39, 49): the legacy stream "synchronizes with all other streams in the same CUcontext except for non-blocking streams".
findings.fix: Use cuMemsetD8Async on the agent's own stream followed by cuStreamSynchronize at registration, which is still before any capture. Completion then synchronizes with the return of the stream synchronization, and later launches are ordered by "Start of a CUDA API call to enqueue a task synchronizes with start of the task".

findings.title: The status lookup's acquire fence comes before the read and pairs with nothing; the tool's plain copies race with the agent's atomic stores
findings.scenario: A tool polls key max_entries+1 until FINAL==1, then looks up the values. The fence is issued before the syscall server copies the status word with plain loads, so it synchronizes with nothing. Under the documented C++ model nothing orders the tool's later data reads after its observation of FINAL==1. On aarch64 the plain FINAL load may be satisfied after the later acquire load of DELIVERIES, so the tool can treat pre-final values as final. The window is sub-microsecond. The plain memcpy of data words while the next delivery stores them (relaxed atomics) is also a data race in C++ terms.
findings.evidence: `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire); return status_buffer.data() + 8 * (k - max_entries);`. C++ [atomics.fences] (cxx-draft-atomics-fences.txt:37): an acquire fence B synchronizes only "if there exists some atomic operation X on M such that X is sequenced before B". [intro.races] (:264-266): a race with a non-atomic access "results in undefined behavior".
findings.fix: Read status words with `__atomic_load_n(..., __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` into a per-thread buffer and return that buffer. For data lookups, keep the acquire load of DELIVERIES and copy the words with relaxed atomic loads into a per-thread buffer, instead of returning the shared pointer.

notes:
Review was read-only: nothing was built or run, and no files were written. Verdicts per claim:

(a) Holds. Sources:
- PTX 5.1.5: ".local ... private memory for each thread"; under the ABI, .local variables are "declared within function scope and are allocated on the stack".
- PTX 6.4.1.1: a generic address in the local window maps to the thread's local memory.
- PTX 7.1 (ptx-isa.txt:6986) and call (25911): "Arguments may be registers".
- CPG 2.3.3.4: "Local memory is used for thread local storage during the execution of a kernel".
- Preemption is still only partly documented (step0b claim 6). An atomic on that memory is not documented (finding 1).

(b) Holds, but by same-thread program order (PTX 8.9.5: "X precedes Y in program order"), not by equal width. The premise is false in the pass output: the area is zeroed with st.u64, the program accesses it with two ld.u32/st.u32 (6lQrMe:2582-2583, 2755-2757), and helper 2 copies byte by byte (simple_memcpy). Same-thread operations are in causality order, so there is no race.

(c) Holds only for XADD.DW. emitAtomicBinOp lowers it (Monotonic) to atom.add.u64, which defaults to .relaxed .gpu (26577/26579), on the same virtual address as the snapshot's ld.relaxed.gpu.u64, so PTX 8.7 and the single-copy atomicity rule apply. Other accesses (finding 2) and other domains (finding 5) fall outside.

(d) Documented by PTX 8.5: .gpu "also includes other kernel grids invoked by the host program on the same compute device". Unlike step0b C5 claim 5 (a copy against a running kernel, which is not documented), a kernel's morally strong loads are inside the memory model.

(e) Holds. PTX API synchronization: "Completion of the last task queued to a stream, if any, synchronizes with return from cudaStreamSynchronize", and API synchronization "also participate[s] in proxy-preserved base causality order", which covers a host/device alias. A cuMemHostGetDevicePointer failure is logged and the map is not registered.

(f) The data path's release fetch_add / acquire load pairing is correct. The status path is not (finding 7).

(g) Conditional (finding 3). The documented chain (kernel end, then the application's stream sync, then the exiting thread's later cuLaunchKernel) exists only if the application synchronized before exit.

(h) Holds:
- %smid is masked with pow2-1, so any value, including non-contiguous ids, stays in range.
- %laneid is 0..WARP_SZ-1, and "to date, all target architectures have a WARP_SZ value of 32" (ptx-isa.txt:2454).
- The shard count hardcodes 32 instead of reading CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_WARP_SIZE; `lane & 31` would remove even that assumption.

Outside this dimension, not reported as a finding: every GPU process sharing one segment writes its own totals into the same shared 1531/1532 copy and into the `shards` field. Each delivery overwrites the others; the comment says "one GPU process per segment", but nothing detects it.

findings.title: Atomic adds on a thread-local (1530) value become generic atom/red on a .local address, which the PTX ISA leaves undefined
findings.scenario: A program written the usual eBPF way, like the repo's GPU examples (threadhist-gpu-kernel-shared-map: `__atomic_add_fetch(cnt, 1, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST)`; threadscheduling: `__sync_fetch_and_add(...)`), with its map switched to 1530: `u64 *v = bpf_map_lookup_elem(&tl, &k); if (v) __sync_fetch_and_add(v, 1);`. The routed lookup returns a cvta.local generic address (the trampoline path does the same through thread_local_offset). llvmbpf lowers the BPF atomic to a generic `atom.add.u64 [%rdX], 1` (or `red`), and %rdX now points into the local window. PTX ISA 9.7.15.5/9.7.15.6 allow scalar atom/red only on .global/.shared, or on generic addresses that point there. The outcome is undefined; on hardware it is likely an illegal-address or illegal-instruction exception in the application's kernel, and the application's CUDA context is then lost. Nothing rejects or rewrites this. The prototype's checks (pt_lat, pt_carry) use only plain loads and stores on 1530 values, so they never exercised it.
findings.evidence: Routing (line 206ff) emits `cvta`-based addresses: `add.u64 %bptl_aN, %bptl_aN, %bpftime_tl_in; ... selp.b64 RET, %bptl_aN, 0, %bptl_pN;` where %bpftime_tl_in comes from the kernel's `cvta.local.u64 %bpftime_tl, __bpftime_tl;`. Trampoline default_trampoline.cu:249-256 `return (char *)(uintptr_t)area + (uintptr_t)info.extra_buffer + idx * info.value_size;`. Lowering seen in lat4 patched PTX (FMPp62 line 2678): `atom.add.u64 %rd56, [%rd55], 1;` on a helper-1 result. ptx-isa.txt:26571: "atom with scalar type may be used only with .global and .shared spaces and with generic addressing, where the address points to .global or .shared space." red: ptx-isa.txt:27027, same rule. CUDA guide (cpg-cpp-language-extensions.txt:1983): atomics act on words "stored in global or shared memory". `git diff 52126f33..HEAD` has no handling of atom/red/isspacep for 1530.
findings.fix: In every probe function (routed and unrouted), rewrite each generic `atom.*`/`red.*` so it first tests the address with `isspacep.local` (a documented instruction). Local addresses take a plain ld/op/st, which is exact because the memory is the thread's own; other addresses keep the original atomic. Alternatively, define and enforce at load that 1530 values allow only plain loads and stores, with a counted refusal. Add a check program that uses __sync_fetch_and_add and __atomic_add_fetch on a 1530 value.

findings.title: Size of the thread-local area has no bound: one zeroing store per 8 bytes in every probed kernel; large maps stall or OOM the host in the load hook or fail application launches
findings.scenario: Creating a 1530 map accepts any size (nv_gpu_thread_local_map_impl's constructor checks nothing). The area is the sum of ALL 1530 maps in the handler table, including other tools' maps, and goes into every probed kernel of every patched module. Examples: (a) max_entries=1<<20, value 8: area 8 MB. Routing builds 1M `st.u64` lines (~25 MB of PTX) per probed kernel, inside the application's cuLibraryLoadData hook, under load_substitution_mutex. nvPTXCompiler then rejects the module anyway, because local memory is limited to 512 KB per thread, and the whole fatbin loads without probes after a long stall. (b) Larger maps: tens of GB of string, so bad_alloc, or the OOM killer takes the host process (8 GB Orin), which breaks the host contract. (c) max_entries >= 2^31 is stored in MapBasicInfo.max_entries (int) as a negative number and sign-extended to ~2^64 at line 981; the area wraps near UINT64_MAX and the zeroing loop does not end until memory runs out. (d) Areas that compile (e.g. 64 KB) still need area x resident threads of local memory per launch (~768 MB on 8 SMs x 1536 threads). The application's launches can then fail with out-of-memory or out-of-resources errors, even for kernels whose programs use no 1530 map.
findings.evidence: nv_attach_impl.cpp:981-982 `d.max_entries = (uint64_t)m.max_entries; area = std::max(area, d.offset + d.value_size * d.max_entries);` (MapBasicInfo::max_entries is `int`; get_max_entries() returns uint32_t). nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:257 `area_bytes = std::max<uint64_t>(8, (area_bytes + 7) & ~7ull);` and 330-332 `for (uint64_t off = 0; off < area_bytes; off += 8) decl << "\tst.u64 \t[" << AREA_REG << "+" << off << "], 0;\n";`. nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:21-26: the 1530 constructor stores value_size/max_entries without checks.
findings.fix: Bound the area up front. Refuse to create a 1530 map whose value_size*max_entries is above a small documented limit (well under 512 KB, minus the probe stack), and make routing skip with a logged, counted refusal when the sum is over the limit, before generating any text. Read max_entries as uint32 (or check it is non-negative) before widening. Zero with a loop (a counter and a branch) instead of one store per word. Optionally give each kernel only the maps its own programs reference.

findings.title: Direct-run path (bpf_main as a kernel) is not routed: helper calls keep an undefined r5, which the 1530 trampoline treats as an area address instead of returning NULL
findings.scenario: `bpftimetool` runs a CUDA program directly through run_attach_entry_on_gpu, and the program uses a 1530 map. bpf_main is compiled without route_thread_local_maps, so param4 of each helper-1/2 call stays the program's leftover or undefined register (in pass output such registers are never defined, e.g. `st.param.b64 [param4+0], %rd23;`). map_info, written with the 1530 entries at lines 1377-1390, routes the call to thread_local_offset(idx, info, c). Any non-zero c returns c + offset + idx*value_size: a wild generic pointer, not NULL. The program's store or load through it corrupts memory or faults the context. The routing header's claim ("Probe functions no routed kernel calls ... pass 0 there: their thread-local lookups return NULL") does not hold for this path.
findings.evidence: nv_attach_impl.cpp:1274-1280 `wrap_ptx_with_trampoline_for_sm(filter_compiled_ptx_for_ebpf_program(ptxpass::compile_ebpf_to_ptx_from_words(ebpf_words, sm_arch.c_str(), "bpf_main", false, false), "bpf_main"), sm_arch)` with no routing call. default_trampoline.cu:282-286: `if (map_info.map_type == BPF_MAP_TYPE_GPU_THREAD_LOCAL_ARRAY_MAP) { ... return (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)thread_local_offset(real_key, map_info, c); }` and 252: `if (area == 0 || idx >= ...) return nullptr;`, so only an exact 0 gives NULL. nv_thread_local_routing.hpp:9-11 states the 0 contract.

notes:
I only read the code (git diff/show, grep, sed). Nothing was built or run, and nothing touched the GPU. Shapes I checked against real pass output: lat4 FMPp62 patched PTX (kprobe+kretprobe on one llama.cpp kernel, routed) and the step0b C1 kmr kernel (@p ret, @p exit, exit, ret, `$L: call ...` on one line, label on the previous line, nested blocks).

Checked and found sound, so not reported:
(1) Label and predicate handling. The label stays on the cvta and the predicate on the call. A cvta placed before an earlier predicated branch on the same line is harmless, because %bpftime_tl only ever holds one value and its kernel-top assignment (before any label) dominates every site. "Area address skipped by a branch" therefore cannot happen.
(2) Probe-name prefixes across kernels (kmr/kmr_d, foo/foo_bar). Both the site scan and the safety check need ';' right after the exact name. __retprobe_func__K does not contain __probe_func__K.
(3) Calls the safety check misses (multi-line or argument-list forms, stub-path calls in device functions) still have the wrong argument count. ptxas rejects them, the module fails to compile, and the original image loads, so nothing goes wrong silently.
(4) Zeroing comes before the entry call. Both are inserted at the first '{', ahead of any label.
(5) Offsets in bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp: 1530 maps in handler-index order, each rounded to 8. The routing area is the max of offset + vs*me, rounded to 8. Both index the same map_basic_info vector by fd, so they agree.
(6) The direct lookup (u32 key, setp.lt.u32 bound, mul.wide + area + offset, selp NULL) matches the trampoline. In LLVM 15 output, callseq blocks contain only param lines (scan of all lat4 files), so replacing a whole block drops no live definitions.
(7) Every routing exception (runtime_error, regex_error, out_of_range from stoll, bad_alloc) is caught in the pool task. hack_fatbin returns nullopt and the fatbin loads unprobed, as the header documents. Note that one routing failure drops every program's probes in that fatbin, even programs that use no 1530 map.
(8) constant_fd's list of defining opcodes (mov|ld|add|sub|cvt|selp|mul|and|or|shl|shr, unanchored) misses mad, neg, not, min/max, div/rem, atom and vector-load destinations ({%rdN,...}). A register defined once by a constant mov and also by one of these would be taken as a constant fd. Clang-compiled eBPF never merges a map-pointer constant with such a value, so I did not count this as a real defect. Being conservative (every textual occurrence of the register other than the mov and the param0 store disqualifies it) would close it.
(9) The routing depends on LLVM 15's printing (`[paramN+0]`, `{ // callseq`, `[retval0+0]`). If a newer LLVM drops "+0", routing throws and the fatbin loads unprobed, which is safe. The build uses /usr/lib/llvm-15.
(10) Upstream issues the routing does not change: two programs of the same probe kind on one kernel give duplicate __probe_func__K definitions; memcapture numbering restarts per pass; memcapture inserts calls inside callseq blocks, and a direct lookup drops the ones inside its own block (synthetic param lines only).
